research_question: from the same complete deployable state, do short q1/q2 coordination biases cause repeatable meaningful differences in future measured cumulative cuff force when task timing is comparable

matched_units.bias_semantics: phase-relative total-action perturbation; hip-leading advances q1 and retards q2, knee-leading does the reverse, balanced is exactly zero

timing_contract.comparison_if_timing_gate_fails: BR-B unless snapshot validity itself fails

decision_rules.BR-A: all validity and timing gates pass, every anchor has repeatable best-branch identity in at least two of three seeds, and both integral and mean-force separation gates pass
decision_rules.BR-B: snapshots and executions are valid, but differences are too small, not repeatable, or timing comparability fails
decision_rules.BR-C: snapshot equality, fixed-condition isolation, branch feasibility, artifact completeness, or experiment execution validity fails

future_shadow_value_if_br_a.dataset_unit: complete rollout with matched-group and trajectory identifiers
future_shadow_value_if_br_a.target: remaining integral of deployable measured cuff-force norm to required task completion with existing non-success penalty
future_shadow_value_if_br_a.split: complete matched seed-anchor groups, never adjacent frames
future_shadow_value_if_br_a.primary_validation: held-out within-group path ranking plus baseline progress/time predictor
future_shadow_value_if_br_a.ood_rule: unsupported prediction cannot receive an attractive low value
